title: Worker execution context
description: The dispatch contract for exactly one worker: one work item, one branch, one pull request, one explicit contract. Required by spec/governance/agent-dispatch.md and machine-validated by scripts/validate_governance.py, which validates the embedded examples against this schema.

repository.description: Repository identity in owner/name form, for example payswapdotorg/payswap3.

base_sha.description: Exact current main SHA at dispatch time: full 40 lowercase hexadecimal characters. The worker builds on exactly this SHA and records it in every report; base movement arrives only via sibling-wave updates or re-dispatch.

work_item_id.description: Identifier of the single assigned work item, for example GOV-001 or PROD-014.

architecture_authority.description: Path of the authoritative architecture for this work item, for example spec/architecture/v0.1/.

hard_dependencies.description: Work item IDs that must be MERGED (a Git fact) before implementation starts; never inferred from projections.

contract_dependencies.description: Contracts the work item must conform to: repository paths or work item IDs.

owned_surfaces.description: Path prefixes that are the only surfaces the worker may create or modify. At least one is required; a prefix reserves every path beneath it.

forbidden_surfaces.description: Path prefixes the worker must not create, modify, or delete under any circumstances.

assurance_profile.description: Name of the evidence standard that applies to this work item, resolved per spec/governance/agent-dispatch.md (required tests, proofs, journey evidence).

required_proofs.description: Concrete, checkable proofs the worker must deliver. At least one is required.

dogfooding_requirements.description: Journey evidence required by spec/governance/dogfooding-protocol.md; empty only when the assurance profile explicitly contains no dogfooding component.

checkpoint_contract.description: When and how the worker must report: checkpoints, report format, and escalation timing.

stop_conditions.description: Conditions that halt implementation and trigger escalation per spec/governance/drift-control.md. At least one is required.

required_proofs: python3 scripts/validate_governance.py exits 0 from the repository root with a summary line per check
dogfooding_requirements: Run the validator as the governance dogfooding journey and capture its output as evidence
examples.checkpoint_contract: Report at completion using the work order report format; escalate immediately on any stop condition or any classification other than WITHIN_SCOPE.
stop_conditions: The provided repository facts are internally contradictory (ARCHITECTURE_BLOCKER)

required_proofs: Journey transcript for the checkout workflow answering all nine reconciliation questions
Unit and integration tests green for every changed surface
dogfooding_requirements: Exercise the checkout journey on the real composed system in the sandbox; mark every financial execution as sandbox-only
examples.checkpoint_contract: Report at start with the journey plan, at the mid-point checkpoint with progress, and at completion with the full evidence bundle.
stop_conditions: Any drift classification other than WITHIN_SCOPE
A missing protocol capability required by the product journey
